deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page and nothing to derive. It is a bibliographic note in Riemann's hand, reading list on the Herbart controversy (top right: archival pencil 'Riemann 18'; circled folio number 70 at right margin). Content, restated:

(1) Berliner Monatsberichte (Monatsberichte der Königlich Preußischen Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Berlin) 1856. Session of the philosophisch-historische Klasse, 18 February: F. A. Trendelenburg, 'Über Herbarts Metaphysik und neue Auffassungen derselben. Zweiter Artikel. Eine Entgegnung' (a reply).

(2) In parentheses, the works the reply is directed against (the opening abbreviation is probably 'g.' = 'gegen'):
- Moritz Wilhelm Drobisch, 'Synechologische Untersuchungen', in I. H. Fichte's Zeitschrift für Philosophie und philosophische Kritik, vol. XXV, no. 2 (1854) and vol. XXVI, no. 1 (1855). Synechology is Herbart's metaphysical theory of continuity: space, time, motion, matter.
- Ludwig Strümpell, 'Einige Worte über Herbart's Metaphysik in Rücksicht auf die Beurtheilung derselben durch Herrn Prof. Trendelenburg'.

(3) 'cf.' Trendelenburg's first article: Monatsberichte, Nov. 1853, pp. 654 ff. It was reprinted in vol. 2 of Trendelenburg's 'Historische Beiträge zur Philosophie', Berlin 1855, pp. 313 ff.

(4) Drobisch in the Zeitschrift, vol. XIV, p. 90: an earlier Drobisch article in the same journal.

Purpose: Riemann was tracking the 1853–56 debate between Trendelenburg and the Herbartians (Drobisch, Strümpell) over Herbart's metaphysics and synechology. That debate concerns the philosophical foundations of continuous magnitude, space and time. The note fits his known Herbartian leanings and the philosophical background to his 1854 Habilitationsvortrag on the hypotheses of geometry and to his Naturphilosophie fragments.

results.what: Bibliographic reading note on the Trendelenburg–Drobisch–Strümpell controversy over Herbart's metaphysics and synechology (1853–1856)

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann's engagement with Herbart is well documented (e.g. his statement that he was a Herbartian in psychology and epistemology, and the Naturphilosophie fragments in the Werke). Seeing him follow the specific 1856 Trendelenburg reply and Drobisch's synechological studies is a minor contextual detail. It is of mild interest for the background of his views on continuous manifolds, but it contains no mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Opening of the parenthesis: the image reads '(g.' or '(z.' rather than '(Z.'. It is most likely 'g.' = 'gegen', since Trendelenburg's article is a reply against Drobisch and Strümpell.
'f. Ph. u. ph.'sche Kritik' abbreviates 'für Philosophie und philosophische Kritik' (title of I. H. Fichte's Zeitschrift).
Top-right pencil 'Riemann 18' is an archival marking; the circled '70' at the right margin is the folio number. Neither should be read as part of the text.
Closing quotation mark after 'Trendelenburg' has no matching opening mark in the manuscript (Riemann's own inconsistency, not a transcription error).
